Required findings: Patient diagnosed with primary, localized uveal melanoma.
Patient has undergone a biopsy of the primary tumor.
Molecular/chromosomal testing for prognostication was performed on the biopsy sample.
The results of the molecular/chromosomal testing were used to determine the class of the tumor (Class 1A, Class 1B, or Class 2).
The class determination is based on the findings from the guidelines and evidence provided in Section S3.18.3.

Non-Indications: Testing for DecisionDx Uveal Melanoma is not medically necessary if the patient does not have a diagnosis of primary, localized uveal melanoma.
Testing for DecisionDx Uveal Melanoma is not medically necessary if the patient has not undergone a biopsy of the primary tumor.
Testing for DecisionDx Uveal Melanoma is not medically necessary if molecular/chromosomal testing for prognostication was not performed on the biopsy sample.
Testing for DecisionDx Uveal Melanoma is not medically necessary if the results of the molecular/chromosomal testing were not used to determine the tumor class (Class 1A, Class 1B, or Class 2).
Testing for DecisionDx Uveal Melanoma is not medically necessary if the class determination was not based on the findings from the guidelines and evidence provided in Section S3.18.3.

Testing for DecisionDx Uveal Melanoma is not medically necessary if the patient has a diagnosis of metastatic uveal melanoma (as the test is designed to assess risk of metastasis within 5 years, not manage metastatic disease).
Testing for DecisionDx Uveal Melanoma is not medically necessary if the patient has a diagnosis of non-ocular melanoma.
Testing for DecisionDx Uveal Melanoma is not medically necessary if the test is considered Experimental, Investigational, or Unproven (E/I/U) based on Section S3.18.5.
Important criteria & exceptions: The test is considered Experimental, Investigational, or Unproven (E/I/U) as per Section S3.18.5.
The test is not generally accepted as the standard of care in the evaluation or management of a particular condition.
FDA approval or clearance is not a reliable standard for this type of laboratory testing.
Clinical validity and clinical utility studies are lacking for DecisionDx Uveal Melanoma.
No conclusions can be drawn regarding the value and usefulness of DecisionDX-PRAME based on insufficient evidence (Section S3.18.3).
Documentation required: Patient diagnosis confirmation document (e.g., pathology report, radiology report confirming primary uveal melanoma).
Biopsy specimen documentation (e.g., surgical procedure report, pathology report detailing the biopsy).
Molecular/chromosomal testing results report for DecisionDx Uveal Melanoma.
Provider notes documenting the use of the molecular/chromosomal test results to determine the tumor class (Class 1A, Class 1B, or Class 2).
